content_preview.title: VS Code 1.139 Ships Dev Container Agent Sessions and Cuts Session-List Load Times Up to 12x
content_preview.summary: Visual Studio Code 1.139 extends Dev Container agent sessions to remote hosts and speeds up large agent session lists by up to 12x, Microsoft says.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Microsoft released [Visual Studio Code 1.139](https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_139) as a stable build on September 23, 2026, speeding up how the editor loads and refreshes large agent session lists and extending Dev Container support for AI agents to remote projects. The release's [tagged entry on GitHub](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/releases/tag/1.139.0) confirms the same date, showing the 1.139.0 tag published September 23 at 10:32 UTC. editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (533 words) following the standard Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis format. Neutral, technical register throughout, no editorializing or sensationalism.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both cited sources were read from the committed gzip snapshots in sources/2026-09/vs-code-1139-ships-dev-container-agent-sessions-and-cuts-session-list-load-times-up-to-12x/ (sha256 of both decompressed files matched manifest.json exactly, confirming integrity). source-0.html.gz (code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_139, HTTP 200): confirmed verbatim -- release highlights line 'This release makes large agent session lists faster, extends Dev Container support to remote projects, and improves everyday editing.'; the faster-session-list quote and the performance table itself: 'First session listing after launch: 1.3 seconds -> 0.1 seconds -> About 12x faster' and 'Refresh the session list: 0.6 seconds -> 0.15 seconds -> About 4x faster' (measured by Microsoft on ~645 sessions on a dev machine, a caveat the article correctly omits from the raw number but implicitly covers in 'What We Don't Know'); the Dev Container remote-host quote verbatim ('Let agents build and test your remote project... This release extends Dev Container sessions from local folders to projects on SSH, Tunnel, and WSL hosts.'); the Compact View, word-wrap-indicator, and bracket-auto-closing quotes all verbatim; and the page header confirms 'Released September 23, 2026 Stable'. source-1.html.gz (github.com/microsoft/vscode/releases/tag/1.139.0, HTTP 200): confirmed page title 'Release 1.139.0 - microsoft/vscode - GitHub' and a <time datetime> attribute of 2026-09-23T10:32:34Z, matching the article's 'tag published September 23 at 10:32 UTC' to the minute. No snapshot fetch failures; no WebFetch fallback was needed.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quote in the article body (release-highlights summary line, session-list catalog explanation, Dev Container remote-host passage, Compact View description, word-wrap-indicator description, bracket-closing description) was located verbatim in source-0's extracted text -- no paraphrase-inside-quotes, no hallucinated quotes. The two headline performance multipliers (12x and 4x) are Microsoft's own stated figures ('About 12x faster' / 'About 4x faster'), not the bot's derived math, and they match the raw before/after seconds in the release-notes table exactly. The internal link to the prior VS Code 1.132 article (/article/2026-08/07-vs-code-1132-ships-agent-host-architecture-browser-element-comments-and-on-device-multilingual-dictation) resolves to an existing file. No fabricated specifics found.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Attributions are consistently hedged with 'Microsoft says' / 'according to the release notes' rather than stated as independent fact, which is appropriate for a vendor release-notes-only story with no independent verification of the performance benchmark.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/2026-09/ and the wider archive for prior VS Code 1.139 coverage; none exists. Other September articles that mention 'VS Code' do so only in passing (e.g. GitHub Copilot integration pieces) and do not cover this release. The immediately prior VS Code release article (1.132, published 2026-08-07) covers different subject matter (Agent Host architecture, browser element comments, on-device dictation) -- no topic overlap or redundancy.
editor_notes.suspicious_patterns_check: manifest.json records suspicious_patterns: null for both sources -- the regex scanner found no matches. Independently re-read both full extracted texts; no prompt-injection-style or AI-directed text was present in either snapshot.
editor_notes.human_requested_check: human_requested is false in the submission; the heightened-scrutiny human-requested checklist does not apply, though the requested extra scrutiny on the two numeric performance claims and the Dev Container remote-host claim was performed and both check out (see source_verification above).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Clean, accurately sourced release-notes report. Both flagged claims for extra scrutiny -- the 12x/4x session-list performance figures and the Dev Container local-to-remote (SSH/Tunnel/WSL) extension -- are verbatim from Microsoft's own release notes and are not exaggerated or misattributed by the bot. Ready for publication as-is.
